rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for going around a physical obstacle and can also mean bypassing a procedure.

example.english: We bypass downtown and go straight to the pier.
example.traditional: 我哋繞過市中心，直接去碼頭。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 jiu5 gwo3 si5 zung1 sam1 zik6 zip3 heoi3 maa5 tau4

rows.note: Use this colloquial phrase when the bypass specifically means taking a detour or another road around an obstacle.

example.english: We bypass the traffic jam by taking the Western Harbour Crossing before going home.
example.traditional: 前面塞死咗，我哋兜路行西隧先返到屋企。
example.jyutping: cin4 min6 sak1 sei2 zo2 ngo5 dei6 dau1 lou6 haang4 sai1 seoi6 sin1 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2

rows.note: Use this when bypass means skipping the normal steps or channels rather than physically going around something.

example.english: They bypass the procedure to approve the application quickly, and end up causing complaints.
example.traditional: 佢哋為咗盡快批出申請，跳過程序，結果惹起投訴。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 wai6 zo2 zeon6 faai3 pai1 ceot1 san1 cing2 tiu3 gwo3 cing4 zeoi6 git3 gwo2 je5 hei2 tau4 sou3
